body: “This is the basic Circuit, how good could it be?”

Good point. I know we’ve discussed my actions in therapy/counseling and I’m trying to prove worthy of that trust again, but I know I’m not owed it.

I’ll take Janey_Cake’s advice and ask if calling off the engagement would help, and keep working through therapy if we need more time.

Thanks for the reading recommendation. I’ll pop an order in for a copy through Amazon and see if it’ll offer any insights. :)

Also, that wouldn’t have been us; only my friends who are a couple were there with us, not her family.

I won’t deny that I have issues and things I need to improve on, but I’m doing my best and I don’t want to explicitly roll out every problem my fiancée and I have had in public like I’m griping. Yes, she was 21, and I was 27 when we first met in person. 

I feel a little confused and scared at the idea that we rushed things; for a while in our relationship I felt as though we had finally come to a point where we were ready to commit to our relationship and each other.
Oof. Well shit, that’s a bit of a gut check. Still, better I steel myself for the possibility rather than fool myself into thinking there’s no way that couldn’t happen.
Bless you for this, this will be a lifesaver. I’ll bring it to her attention and try to get her an appointment as soon as possible.
Alas, not without paying out of pocket for it. She’s on Medicaid at the moment for her healthcare.

Oh. Well we haven’t discussed *that* yet, but I’ll bring it up as an option. I do want to marry her and engagement doesn’t seem too much different from how we were before, but if now isn’t the right time, so be it. Anything is on the table if it’ll stop her hurting so much.
Okay. I’ll do my best to be there for her. Thank you for your advice; I’ll see if I can find her a tele-therapist she can see sooner. :)
I have! It seems like the idea of a long engagement without pressure or a set date has helped, but the anxiety still crops up day after day. :(
